marker: # unit_length is the Average repeat size of Table 1. It is an average because these arrays are
# imperfect: the same table counts the variable bases per locus, from none at VNTR67_01 and
# VNTR21_01 to 23 of 66 at VNTR61_02 and 26 of 81 at VNTR81_01.
# ref_size is the product these primers give in the N315 assembly GCA_000009645.1 by in silico
# PCR. Every locus gives exactly one product with no primer mismatch, and all eight lengths equal
# the span of the coordinates Table 2 gives in NC_002745 for the same primer pair, which is an
# exact independent check of both the primers and the coordinates.
# ref_repeats IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY, SO THIS SCHEME SIZES ITS MARKERS WITHOUT CALLING THEM.
# The paper derives an allele as the product length minus the flanking length, divided by the
# repeat size, but it publishes neither the flanking length nor the repeat unit sequences, and it
# does not state the repeat number of the sequenced reference. Counting the arrays in N315 to
# recover them was tried and is not dependable here: the repeats are too imperfect, so a tandem
# finder reports no array at all for VNTR67_01 and VNTR81_01, a 4 bp unit unrelated to the locus
# for VNTR61_02, and copy numbers for the rest that disagree with its own estimates. A wrong
# reference count would shift every allele at that locus by a constant and would be invisible in
# the output, so no count is recorded rather than a doubtful one.
# To enable calling, supply either the flanking lengths, which fix ref_repeats for the measured
# sizes above, or the published size to allele table as bins.tsv. Table 1 bounds what to expect:
# the repeat range over the 1681 isolates is 6-25 for VNTR09_01, 0-6 VNTR61_01, 0-5 VNTR61_02,
